blocks.text: 1. The Decoder

blocks.alt: The encoder output goes through stacked decoder layers to an output sequence

blocks.text: The Encoder, the previous topic, read the entire input sequence into rich, context-aware representations. The Decoder is the Transformer's own output-generating half, explored throughout this topic.

It produces the output sequence one position at a time, using both Self-Attention and Cross-Attention, both already covered in the Attention Mechanism module, a genuinely essential complementary half covered throughout this topic.
2. Recapping The Handoff From The Encoder

This connects back to the encoder output feeds into the decoder, already covered in The Encoder. The encoder's own genuinely final output, already covered there, becomes the decoder's own Key and Value.
This topic genuinely explores exactly how the decoder itself actually works, building directly on that exact handoff already covered at the end of the previous topic.
3. The Decoder Layer Structure

blocks.alt: Masked self-attention feeds cross-attention, then a feed-forward layer

blocks.text: This connects back to the encoder layer structure, already covered in The Encoder. Each decoder layer genuinely has three parts: Self-Attention, Cross-Attention, and a feed-forward network.
This is one genuinely additional component beyond the encoder's own two-part structure already covered there, a genuinely direct structural expansion covered throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Self-Attention Within The Decoder

blocks.alt: Previous tokens only feed into masked self-attention

blocks.text: This connects back to Self-Attention, already covered in the Attention Mechanism module. The decoder genuinely attends to its own genuinely already-generated output positions.

This lets each new prediction genuinely take into account everything generated so far, applying the exact same Self-Attention mechanism already covered there, now within the decoder's own growing output sequence.
5. Cross-Attention To The Encoder

blocks.alt: A decoder query attends to the encoder key and value

blocks.text: This connects back to Cross-Attention, already covered in its own topic. The decoder genuinely then attends to the encoder's own output, using the exact framework already covered there.
This uses the exact Query-from-decoder, Key-and-Value-from-encoder pattern already covered there, directly connecting the decoder's own generation process back to the entire encoded input.
6. A Preview Of Why Order Genuinely Matters Here

A genuinely important, real structural detail connects forward to Causal Masking, covered later in this module. The decoder's own Self-Attention genuinely must not look ahead at future, not-yet-generated positions.

This genuinely necessary constraint, already covered in this section, is explored in complete mathematical detail in that later topic, a genuinely essential rule for correct, honest sequence generation.

blocks.title: warning
blocks.content: Without this constraint, already covered in this topic, the decoder could genuinely "cheat" during training by looking at future words it is supposed to be predicting, producing a genuinely broken, unrealistic model.

blocks.text: 7. Recapping Sequential Generation

blocks.alt: Token 1, 2, and 3 are generated in sequence

blocks.text: This connects back to sequential word generation, already covered in Image Captioning. At inference time, the decoder genuinely still generates output one position at a time.

This happens even though the underlying Attention computations, already covered, can process in parallel during training, a genuinely important distinction between training-time and inference-time behavior.
8. The Final Output Layer

blocks.alt: A decoder output goes through a linear and softmax layer to next token probabilities

blocks.text: This connects back to Softmax, already covered in the Activation Functions module. The genuinely final decoder layer's own output genuinely passes through Softmax to produce a probability over the vocabulary.
This is the exact same final decision mechanism already covered throughout Image Classification and Image Captioning, applied here to select the next genuinely predicted word.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When The Decoder Is Genuinely Necessary

blocks.alt: Needing to generate text points toward using a decoder

blocks.text: This connects back to Machine Translation and Image Captioning, both already covered, needing genuinely sequential output. The decoder, already covered in this topic, directly generates that genuinely sequential output.

This connects forward to Large Language Models, covered later in this course, built around genuinely decoder-focused designs. Understanding the decoder now, already covered, is genuinely essential preparation.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simplified decoder layer, combining Self-Attention over generated output with Cross-Attention to encoder output, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 8

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

def attention(query_source, kv_source, rng):
    W_q = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    W_k = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    W_v = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    q, k, v = query_source @ W_q.T, kv_source @ W_k.T, kv_source @ W_v.T
    weights = softmax(q @ k.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size))
    return weights @ v

encoder_output = rng.normal(size=(5, hidden_size))     # already covered as the handoff from The Encoder
decoder_generated_so_far = rng.normal(size=(3, hidden_size))  # already covered as sequential generation

# already covered as Self-Attention within the decoder in this topic
self_attn_output = decoder_generated_so_far + attention(decoder_generated_so_far, decoder_generated_so_far, rng)

# already covered as Cross-Attention to the encoder in this topic
cross_attn_output = self_attn_output + attention(self_attn_output, encoder_output, rng)

print(f"Decoder generated so far shape: {decoder_generated_so_far.shape}")
print(f"After Self-Attention: {self_attn_output.shape}")
print(f"After Cross-Attention to encoder: {cross_attn_output.shape}")
print("\nThis output would then genuinely pass through Softmax, already covered as the final output layer in this topic")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the decoder's own two-step attention process: Self-Attention over its own generated output, then Cross-Attention to the encoder's output, exactly the sequence already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: The Decoder produces the output sequence one position at a time.
Each decoder layer has three parts: Self-Attention, Cross-Attention, and a feed-forward network.
Decoder Self-Attention attends to its own already-generated output positions.
Decoder Cross-Attention attends to the encoder's own final output.
The decoder's Self-Attention must not look ahead at future, not-yet-generated positions.
At inference time, the decoder still generates output one position at a time.
The final decoder output passes through Softmax to produce a probability over the vocabulary.
It is essential for tasks needing sequential output, like translation and captioning.
